units.title: Repeated smallest color classes in odd regular polygons
units.statement: Partition the vertices of an odd regular n-gon into color classes, each itself the full vertex set of an inscribed regular polygon. A class of size m is a residue class modulo d=n/m. For maximal d, summing the d-th roots of unity over all vertices leaves only these smallest classes and gives a vanishing sum of their roots. Since d is odd, at least three such classes are necessary. If n is a power of an odd prime p, the number of smallest classes is a positive multiple of p, and p classes are attainable by residues modulo p.
steps: Represent each regular subpolygon as a coset of a cyclic subgroup
Sum a primitive root of unity for the largest step across the partition
Use oddness to exclude one or two summands; for prime powers evaluate the cyclotomic factor at 1
